name: external-template-library-decisions
body: External template library by path (v1) [with user decisions; autonomous choices flagged]. The deck's library path is stored in `kalide.yaml` under the top-level key `templates:` — chosen over `library:`/`templates-path:` because it reads naturally and collides with no existing key (title/author/date/theme/navigation/properties) [autonomous]. Resolution rule: the configured path wins; else fall back to a local `templates/`; neither = error, no built-in fallback (preserving the project-templates no-fallback ethos); a configured path never silently falls back to a local dir [with user]. A relative path is resolved against the deck root for portability; absolute is allowed [autonomous, as recommended]. Exactly one library per deck: when both a configured path and a local `templates/` exist, the configured path wins and the local dir is ignored (not an error) [autonomous]. `kalide init <path>` points a new deck at an external library: it writes slides/, assets/ and kalide.yaml (with `templates: <path>`) but NOT a local `templates/`, and validates the library at path fail-fast BEFORE writing anything (reusing templates-dir-validation) [autonomous, as recommended]. The no-arg init seed is unchanged. The resolved root is used everywhere a local `templates/` was used: the template-library-loader is the single resolution point for start, the `kalide templates` gallery and live reload, and watch-deck / file-watcher watch the resolved root. Git/network is fully out of scope — kalide never clones or fetches and introduces no credentials or tokens (consistent with global.constraint.anonymous-install). This is the FIRST realization of global.constraint.template-library-shareable: the library stays a self-contained, relocatable unit and its layout is UNCHANGED (library.yaml, slides/, sections/, themes/, media/); only its root becomes resolvable from deck config.
